sections.h2: Which way to sell a Stow house
sections.html:
Let the house's problems pick the route. A well-kept home does fine on the open market, while a dying roof, a difficult tenant or an unfinished estate may point toward a buyer who accepts the place unrepaired.

  • Agent listing: photos, open houses, a buyer's inspection and the repair requests that come after it.
  • Owner-sold: you set the price and handle the disclosure form and deed paperwork.
  • Direct cash sale: one buyer, one walkthrough, and a quicker trip to the county transfer desk.

Each route ends with a deed filed through the county, so bring in a title company or attorney at the beginning.

Stow sits on the Summit and Portage county line next to Akron, on 17.09 square miles of land. Population was estimated at 33,941 on July 1, 2025, down 1.6 percent from April 2020. Owners live in most homes here. The city lies in the secondary Lake Erie snowbelt, so expect an inspector to spend time on the roof, gutters, furnace and basement.

Shoppers here tend to look across the borders too. Kent lies east, Tallmadge and Munroe Falls south, Hudson north and Cuyahoga Falls west, so a Stow listing is usually weighed against houses in those towns. Price against that field and make your photos and description do the work. The 2020 count showed 15,372 housing units, 5.0 percent of them empty. Ohio 8 runs through town, which is worth mentioning in a listing.

They can, when work was left unfinished. If a deck, furnace, roof or basement looks fairly new, a buyer's inspector may ask to see the permit. Dig out your paperwork before listing and finish off anything still open.

Permits and construction inspections come from the Stow Building Department. Its online portal takes forms, inspection requests and contractor registrations at any hour. Call before 9 am for a same-day inspection. Electric and plumbing inspectors visit on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday mornings. The department's phone number is 330-689-2729, and calling it before you list is the quickest way to learn whether anything is unfinished at your address. Engineering covers drawings and work in the public right-of-way, and answers at 330-689-2719.

Sewer permits are a county matter. Summit County's Department of Sanitary Services, 1180 S Main Street in Akron, issues them, so call that office about any sewer lateral question before closing.

sections.h2: What happens at the Summit County Fiscal Office
sections.html:
After closing, the deed goes to the Property Transfer Department in Summit County, where staff check the legal description and approve the conveyance. Each deed carries a DTE 100 statement of value, or a DTE 100 (EX) when an exemption fits. Anything received by 3:30 PM can clear that same day.

The county's fee page lists three charges to expect at closing:

  • The conveyance fee is $4.00 for every $1000 of price, with the price rounded up to the next $100.
  • A lot fee of 50 cents applies to each lot named in the legal description.
  • Recording runs $34.00 for the first two pages, then $8.00 per extra page.

The transfer tax falls on the grantor (Ohio Revised Code 322.02) and is paid to the auditor on delivery of the deed. Have your closing agent match the settlement statement to these three charges.

The state disclosure form is required for a house of up to four units (Ohio Revised Code 5302.30). Sign and date a copy for every prospective buyer and do it early: a buyer who gets it late has the right to rescind in writing. Topics include water, sewer, structure, radon and lead paint.

Answer each question honestly. Where you truly do not know, the statute lets you give a good-faith approximation instead of leaving it blank.

sections.h2: Selling a Stow house with a tenant or from an estate
sections.html:
A tenant can stay through the sale, or the contract can set a move-out date. Either way, hand over the lease and deposit ledger, and keep up your landlord duties until title transfers.

When the house was inherited, the first question is who may sign. The probate court and the Fiscal Office can name the affidavit or certificate that clears the decedent's name, and a probate attorney can cover whatever is left. After that, the sale proceeds in the usual order.

sections.h2: How long a Stow sale can take
sections.html: Time in a sale is mostly spent waiting on other people. A listing waits for showings, a lender and an inspector, and one repair request can reopen the price. Selling on your own is only as quick as your contract and deed are. Cash has the shortest list of steps: one walkthrough, then title work and the Property Transfer Department. On the county side, a clean package filed early may be approved by evening, while a missing form or the wrong fee eats at least a day. Have the closing agent proofread every page before it goes downtown.

sections.h2: Paperwork to line up before closing
sections.html: Collect these before a closing date is set: permit records for every deck, furnace, roof or basement project; a signed and dated disclosure form; the lease, deposit ledger and any move-out date if tenants live there; probate papers if the house came through an estate; and an answer from Summit County Sanitary Services if a sewer lateral is in doubt. Then confirm the three county charges on the settlement statement and settle in writing who pays each one.

sections.h2: When a cash offer is worth considering
sections.html:
Cash makes sense for an inherited house with put-off repairs, a tenant-occupied rental, or an owner who moved away and keeps paying two sets of bills. With a roof or sewer line nearly worn out, selling as is takes the repair decision off your plate.

Judge an offer against what a listing would net after commission and repairs. Pin down who pays the transfer charge, how long title work will take and what happens if the buyer backs out. Every answer belongs in the contract.

faqs.q: Who pays the county transfer charge on a Stow sale?
faqs.a: You do, as the seller. The county transfer tax falls on the grantor under Ohio Revised Code 322.02, and the auditor side of the Summit County Fiscal Office collects it when the deed arrives.

faqs.q: What inspections does the City of Stow perform?
faqs.a: The city inspects permitted construction work and offers same-day visits when you call before 9 am. Nothing here is a mandatory inspection at sale. Ring the Building Department on 330-689-2729 about your address, and assume the buyer will hire a private inspector.

faqs.q: Which office records a Stow deed?
faqs.a: Stow is in Summit County, so the county Fiscal Office records the deed once the transfer is approved. When you set the closing date, ask what the per-page recording charge will be.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Stow house that has a tenant?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the buyer the lease and the deposit ledger, or put a move-out date in the contract. Your landlord duties last until title changes hands.

faqs.q: What if I inherited a house in Stow?
faqs.a: First find out who may legally sign. The probate court and the Fiscal Office can name the affidavit or certificate that clears the decedent's name, and a probate attorney can handle the rest before you accept an offer.
